name: Golf (Nine Card)
description: Nine-Card Golf is a draw-and-discard shedding game played with a 3Ã—3 grid layout where players strategically replace cards to minimize their total score. A unique feature is the ability to score zero by collecting three cards of equal rank in a vertical column, adding a distinctive puzzle element to the Golf family.

content.text: Nine-Card Golf is a draw-and-discard shedding game played with a 3Ã—3 grid layout where players strategically replace cards to minimize their total score. A unique feature is the ability to score zero by collecting three cards of equal rank in a vertical column, adding a distinctive puzzle element to the Golf family.

Nine-Card Golf evolved from the classic Golf family of card games, which emerged in North America in the mid-20th century. The 3Ã—3 grid variant represents an expansion of six-card Golf, introducing more strategic depth through additional card combinations.
One or two standard 52-card decks (one deck sufficient for 2-4 players; two decks for 5-8 players).
Scorepad and pencils for tracking round scores.

Dealer distributes nine cards face-down to each player, one at a time, in clockwise order. Each player arranges their cards in a 3Ã—3 grid (three rows of three cards). Before play begins, each player selects three of their nine cards to turn face-up; the remaining six stay face-down. The remaining deck is placed in the center as the stock, and the top card is flipped face-up beside it to start the discard pile.

items.text: Two Cards Face-Up Start: Only two cards are revealed face-up at the start instead of three. This increases luck and decreases early-game certainty.
Four-Card Bonus: Four cards of identical rank in a 2Ã—2 square (any combination of rows/columns) score negative points (approximately -25). Three-of-a-kind columns still score zero.
Twos as Positive or Joker Rules: House variant: Twos score +2 instead of 2, or jokers (if added to deck) score -2 as wildcards.
Extended Matching (Horizontal/Diagonal): In addition to vertical columns, three-card rows (horizontal) or diagonals also score zero. This increases pattern complexity.
Double-Deck Nine-Card Golf: For 6+ players, use two complete decks (104 cards) to ensure sufficient card variety and prevent running out of needed ranks.
